original_test_intent: Validate the GB FPGA temperature sensor across complete IB/OOB SDR, Sensor List and BMC Web evidence against the approved FPGA thermal specification.
original_method: The hardware/FPGA owner binds the name to the exact device and bitstream, defines die versus board/remote sensing and activity-qualified limits, and permits only passive management and device-state collection.
manual_activity: The FPGA/thermal owner identifies the device, board location, active image and sensing source, approves activity-qualified limits, then reviews complete evidence.
required_inputs: GB board and exact FPGA vendor/device/instance, board coordinate and stable identifier
Active FPGA image/bitstream identity and relevant firmware/CPLD dependency revisions
TEMP_GB_FPGA sensing source: die sensor, internal or remote diode, or board probe
Units, scale, tolerance, resolution, refresh, stale/unavailable, thresholds and hysteresis
Approved ranges by clock/pipeline or fabric activity, power state, airflow and ambient
Passive FPGA configuration/health/status interface and prohibited control registers
SDR entity/name/description plus Sensor List/Web mapping and same-target revisions
Secret-safe collectors and independent FPGA, cooling, BMC and platform recovery
safety_requirements: Bind the reading to the exact FPGA and active bitstream before applying limits
Distinguish die temperature from a nearby board probe and use the matching envelope
Record only passive configuration/activity/health context; do not create a workload or alter clocks
Do not load a bitstream, write FPGA/CPLD controls, reload drivers, change cooling/thresholds/BMC or clear logs
Stop on configuration drift, device fault, invalid/stale reading, thermal event or incomplete evidence
agent_execution_scope: Verify unique source, FPGA physical identity, image identity and sensor source
Collect complete secret-safe IB/OOB SDR/Sensor List, exact sensor result and BMC Web
Collect passive FPGA configuration, health, activity-state, airflow/ambient and SEL context
Compare to owner-approved envelope for the observed image and state
Perform no programming, register write, workload, driver/cooling/threshold/BMC/log mutation, retry or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the GB FPGA instance, board coordinate and active image mapping
Define sensing point, passive activity indicators and thermal envelope
Approve management-view identity and threshold semantics
Review evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES FPGA/IMAGE IDENTITY, SENSOR-LOCATION SEMANTICS AND ACTIVITY-QUALIFIED ENVELOPE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Join the BMC sensor to a stable FPGA device and active image, identify the thermal sensing point, and compare synchronized readings with passive clock/fabric activity and cooling context.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds configuration identity and activity state needed to interpret a generic FPGA temperature.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: PEX switch temperature from the preceding case remains separate and cannot stand in for FPGA thermal evidence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Different bitstreams can enable different transceiver banks, clocks and logic density, changing FPGA power materially; a limit assessed without image and activity identity can accept an overheating configuration or reject an idle-safe one.

project_override_considerations: If the platform has multiple FPGAs or fallback images, each accepted mapping and state requires explicit identity. A configuration change requires fresh evidence, not reuse of the prior temperature verdict.
expected_evidence: Approved FPGA board coordinate/device identifier and active image/bitstream revision
Sensor-source definition, units, freshness, thresholds and image/activity/airflow-qualified limits
Complete redacted IB/OOB SDR and Sensor List plus exact sensor result
BMC Web, same-target proof and passive FPGA configuration/health/activity/ambient/SEL context

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: All source fields consistently target TEMP_GB_FPGA; absent instance, sensing-point and criteria details are project inputs rather than contradictory claims.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The passive exact-sensor purpose is identifiable after the owner supplies FPGA/image identity, sensor semantics and an activity-qualified thermal envelope.

review_improvement: Adds active-image identity and separates FPGA die, remote-diode and board-probe behavior while preserving a strictly read-only scope.
independent_technical_reasoning: FPGA temperature is configuration dependent: enabling transceivers, clocks or dense logic in a different image can shift power without changing the device name. The active bitstream and passive activity state are therefore part of sensor identity for engineering acceptance, not optional diagnostic metadata.
